title_en: Anhui Medical Insurance Company v. (Hong Kong) Huajia Company — application for enforcement of a legally effective civil mediation agreement

full_text_en:
Anhui Provincial Medical Products Import and Export Company v. (Hong Kong) Hua Jia Co., Ltd. — Application for Enforcement of a Legally Effective Civil Mediation Agreement

Applicant for Enforcement: Anhui Provincial Medical Products Import and Export Company.

Legal Representative: Xu Hengbing, General Manager.

Respondent for Enforcement: (Hong Kong) Hua Jia Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Troy D. McBride, Chairman of the Board, citizen of the United States.

The applicant for enforcement, Anhui Provincial Medical Products Import and Export Company (hereinafter referred to as Medical Products Company), applied to the Hefei Intermediate People's Court of Anhui Province for enforcement on the grounds that the respondent, (Hong Kong) Hua Jia Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hua Jia Company), had failed to perform the obligations confirmed by a civil mediation agreement that had become legally effective.

The Hefei Intermediate People's Court found the following facts upon trial: On December 10, 1992, Medical Products Company and Hua Jia Company entered into a sales contract for the export of Heparin Sodium. The contract stipulated: (1) Medical Products Company would export to Hua Jia Company 300 billion units of refined Heparin Sodium in 1993, of which 150 billion units would be exported in June 1993 at an export price of USD 950 per billion units, totaling USD 1,425,000; the delivery time for the remaining Heparin Sodium was to be determined. (2) For the Heparin Sodium purchased by Medical Products Company domestically, the manufacturer must be approved by Hua Jia Company, or the products must be purchased from domestic manufacturers designated by Hua Jia Company. After the contract was signed, within the effective period stipulated in the contract, Medical Products Company performed the contracted supply quantities on two occasions, totaling USD 313,576.16 and RMB 1,625,000 in payment, which Hua Jia Company failed to pay. Thereafter, until the initiation of litigation, the parties reached multiple payment agreements, but Hua Jia Company only paid USD 70,000, leaving the remaining payment always unpaid. Therefore, Medical Products Company filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting that Hua Jia Company repay the principal, interest, and economic losses caused thereby, and bear the litigation costs of the case.

During the litigation, based on Medical Products Company's application for property preservation and guarantee, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court lawfully sealed up the No. 1 factory building of New World Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd., registered by Hua Jia Company in Shenzhen.

After trial, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court presided over mediation, and the parties voluntarily reached the following agreement:

1. The principal and interest in RMB and USD owed by the defendant, (Hong Kong) Hua Jia Co., Ltd., to the plaintiff, Anhui Medical Products Company, totaling RMB 4,100,000, shall be repaid by Hua Jia Company in installments. By October 30, 1994, repay RMB 50,000 and offset RMB 950,000 of the debt with two Mercedes-Benz sedans. The aforesaid RMB 1,000,000 shall no longer bear interest. By December 30, 1994, Hua Jia Company shall repay RMB 2,000,000, offsetting part of the debt with certain goods in Hong Kong (price to be agreed by both parties). If the parties fail to reach an agreement through negotiation, Hua Jia Company shall repay the remaining RMB 3,100,000 in full by July 30, 1995, with interest calculated at a monthly rate of 1%.

2. Until Hua Jia Company fully repays the aforesaid debt, the No. 1 factory building of New World Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd., registered by Hua Jia Company in Shenzhen, shall remain sealed.

After the mediation agreement was served, both parties signed and accepted it, and the mediation agreement became legally effective.

During the performance period of the mediation agreement, the respondent, Hua Jia Company, failed to perform its repayment obligations in accordance with the agreement. On November 1994, the applicant for enforcement, Medical Products Company, filed an application for enforcement with the Hefei Intermediate People's Court pursuant to Article 216, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. On January 9, 1995, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court issued a notice of enforcement to the respondent, Hua Jia Company, in accordance with Article 220 of the Civil Procedure Law.

After the notice of enforcement was issued, Hua Jia Company still failed to perform the mediation agreement. In response, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court issued a summons to summon the respondent to appear in court to explain the reasons for failing to perform the mediation agreement. The respondent still ignored this.

In view of the expiration of the seal on the No. 1 factory building, and to ensure the performance of the mediation agreement, on January 13, 1995, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 223 of the Civil Procedure Law, ruled to continue sealing the No. 1 factory building and impounded two Mercedes-Benz cars, and simultaneously ruled to attach the rent and income from the factory building. Subsequently, the respondent and its agent ad litem were summoned to appear in court on February 16, 1995, to handle matters concerning the enforcement of the mediation agreement. The respondent still did not appear. The Hefei Intermediate People's Court summoned the respondent for a third time to appear in court to explain the reasons for failing to perform the agreement. On March 13 of the same year, the respondent's legal representative, McBride, and agent ad litem, Niu Jialin, appeared in court and submitted a document stating:

1. The two Mercedes-Benz sedans confirmed in the mediation agreement to repay the debt had been separately mortgaged.
2. All assets of New World Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd., originally registered in Shenzhen, had been transferred to a Hong Kong company by way of debt repayment, and the registration was changed in Hong Kong on August 13, 1994.
3. Other creditors in Hong Kong had applied to the High Court of Hong Kong for winding up of Hua Jia Company.

Given that the respondent failed to perform the mediation agreement and there was risk of transferring the impounded property, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court required the respondent to provide valid property security within China, which was refused. Under these circumstances, considering that the respondent's legal representative, McBride, could leave the country at any time, on March 13, 1995, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 23, Item (2) of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Entry and Exit of Aliens, which provides that an alien "shall not be allowed to leave the country if notified by a People's Court of an unresolved civil case," made a decision: "Restrict the departure of Troy D. McBride, Chairman of the Board of (Hong Kong) Hua Jia Co., Ltd."

Subsequently, the respondent's legal representative, McBride, expressed willingness to perform the obligations confirmed by the legally effective civil mediation agreement. On April 5, 1995, the respondent, Hua Jia Company, and the applicant for enforcement, Medical Products Company, reached an agreement regarding the enforcement of the debt: The original mediation agreement confirmed that Hua Jia Company owed Medical Products Company RMB 4,100,000 in principal and interest, plus interest of RMB 279,000 accrued during the litigation period. Hua Jia Company would offset the debt by transferring the No. 1 factory building under the name of New World Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd., registered in Shenzhen, and two Mercedes-Benz sedans at a discounted value. After offsetting the debt with the aforesaid property, the surplus of RMB 3,150,000 would be used by Medical Products Company to repay loan interest, penalty interest, and insurance premiums on behalf of New World Biochemical Technology Co., Ltd. Hua Jia Company would additionally pay RMB 50,000 to Medical Products Company to cover taxes payable during the transfer of the No. 1 factory building.

The aforesaid agreement was performed under the supervision of enforcement officers of the Hefei Intermediate People's Court.

The Hefei Intermediate People's Court subsequently lifted the restriction on the departure of the respondent's legal representative, McBride.
